9. /// </summary>
10. /// <remarks>
11. /// <para>
12. /// This attribute is applied to methods or properties that should be exposed as resources in the Model Context Protocol. When a class
13. /// containing methods marked with this attribute is registered with McpServerBuilderExtensions,
14. /// these methods or properties become available as resources that can be called by MCP clients.
15. /// </para>

20. /// Read resource requests do not contain separate arguments, only a URI. However, for templated resources, portions of that URI may be considered

24. ///     <description>
25. ///       <see cref="CancellationToken"/> parameters are automatically bound to a <see cref="CancellationToken"/> provided by the

28. ///     </description>

34. ///   </item>
35. ///   <item>
36. ///     <description>

39. ///       what server is being used to process the request, and to interact with the client issuing the request to that server.
40. ///     </description>
41. ///   </item>

46. ///       from the resource to the client. If the client included a <see cref="ProgressToken"/> in their request, progress reports issued
47. ///       to this instance will propagate to the client as <see cref="NotificationMethods.ProgressNotification"/> notifications with
48. ///       that token. If the client did not include a <see cref="ProgressToken"/>, the instance will ignore any progress reports issued to it.
